title.narrative: Empowering Women &Youth Smallholder Farmers in Groundnut Market System in F.C.T, Nigeria –Phase 3

description.narrative:
Empowering Women and Youth Smallholder Farmers in Groundnut Market System Development in the Federal Capital Territory, Nigeria – Phase 2, Year 2” is a 12-month intervention implemented by the Centre for Women Studies and Intervention (CWSI) with support from CAFOD. The project will be implemented in Bamishi (Kuje Area Council) and Paiko (Gwagwalada Area Council) of the FCT, Abuja, targeting 150 new women and youth smallholder farmers while consolidating gains from Year 1 beneficiaries.
Building on the successes of earlier phases, the project aims to strengthen economic resilience, improve productivity, enhance market participation, and promote climate-smart agricultural practices within the groundnut value chain. Women and youth farmers in the FCT face systemic challenges including limited access to improved inputs, mechanization, finance, extension services, and structured markets. These constraints reduce productivity and limit income potential.
Year 2 will focus on six strategic priorities: financial literacy and inclusion; introduction of mechanized tools (planters and shellers) to reduce drudgery and improve efficiency; market development through branding and packaging; strengthening cooperative governance and collective marketing; expanding access to gender-responsive credit; and establishing formal extension service linkages.
Through training, provision of improved seeds and equipment, cooperative strengthening, and financial partnerships, the project aims to achieve measurable outcomes including increased groundnut yield and quality, improved financial management skills, enhanced access to credit, greater adoption of value-added processing, and stronger participation in structured markets.
